messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0027051&type=printable
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0027051

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Microfluidic SELEX (M-SELEX) for Rapid Generation of High-Affinity DNA Aptamers Against Protein Targets of Varying Isoelectric Point (PDGF-BB, Thrombin, Apolipoprotein E3)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Randomized ssDNA Library (100-base library, 60 randomized nucleotides flanked by two 20-base PCR primer sites)
  - Target-Coated Magnetic Beads (M-270 carboxylic acid beads with immobilized target protein: PDGF-BB, thrombin, or ApoE)
  - Selection Buffer (PBS + 1 mM MgCl2 + 0.025% Tween 20 for PDGF-BB/ApoE; 50 mM Tris + 100 mM NaCl + 1 mM MgCl2 + 5 mM KCl + 1 mM CaCl2 + 0.025% Tween 20, pH 7.5, for thrombin)
  - Yeast tRNA Blocking Reagent (blocks target-coated beads before rounds 2 and 3)
  - PCR Master Mix and Primers (unlabeled and biotinylated/fluorescently-labeled primers for pool amplification)
  - Lambda Exonuclease (digests the phosphorylated strand to generate single-stranded DNA)

STEPS:
1. Starting pool: Heat-denature the ssDNA library at 95C for 10 minutes, then snap-cool on ice and bring to room temperature.
2. Incubation with target: Incubate the denatured library with washed, target-coated magnetic beads for 1 hour with gentle rotation (blocked with yeast tRNA in rounds 2 and 3).
3. MMS separation: Load the sample onto the micro-magnetic separation (MMS) device; wash at a combined flow rate of 50 mL/hr with selection buffer (6 minutes in round 1, 20 minutes in rounds 2-3, increasing stringency), then elute the aptamer-bound beads with selection buffer.
4. PCR amplification: Amplify the eluted DNA using a biotinylated reverse primer to generate double-stranded DNA, purify, and quantify by UV spectroscopy.
5. Single-strand separation: Digest the double-stranded PCR product with lambda exonuclease to remove the phosphorylated strand and recover the fluorescently-labeled single-stranded forward strand for the next round.
6. Measure pool binding: Incubate a range of concentrations of the fluorescently-labeled ssDNA pool with target-coated beads for 1 hour, wash four times, elute the bound DNA at 95C for 10 minutes, and measure fluorescence in the supernatant to fit a saturation binding curve and determine bulk pool affinity (Kd).
7. Clone and sequence: For pools showing sufficient enrichment/affinity after three rounds, clone into competent E. coli, sequence individual clones, and rank-order them by relative binding signal to identify the highest-affinity individual aptamer sequences (performed off-chip, not modeled).

INTERPRETATION: Successful selection is confirmed by a bulk pool binding affinity (Kd) that decreases (improves) across the three selection rounds, and by individual cloned aptamer sequences exhibiting nanomolar-to-subnanomolar Kd values with negligible binding to non-target proteins or uncoated beads; the paper further reports an inverse relationship between target protein isoelectric point/net charge and aptamer Kd across the three protein targets and under varying selection-buffer pH conditions.

identity.protocol_name: Probing the Limits of Aptamer Affinity with a Microfluidic SELEX Platform (Ahmad, Oh, Kim, McClellen, Xiao & Soh, PLoS ONE 2011)

source.title: Microfluidic SELEX (M-SELEX) for Rapid Generation of High-Affinity DNA Aptamers Against Protein Targets of Varying Isoelectric Point (PDGF-BB, Thrombin, Apolipoprotein E3)

ir.content:
main:
	library1[0] = dispense(ssdna_library)
	heat(library1[0]) @ 95.0CELSIUS @ 600.0SECOND
	heat(library1[0]) @ 4.0CELSIUS @ 120.0SECOND
	beads1[0] = dispense(target_beads)
	selection_mix1[0] = mix(library1[0], beads1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	heat(selection_mix1[0]) @ 23.0CELSIUS @ 3600.0SECOND
bsbbr_2_h:
	PHI REPEAT_51 = {REPEAT_50,REPEAT_52}
	PHI wash1 = {wash0,wash2}
	PHI washed1 = {washed0,washed2}
	if REPEAT_51[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_3_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_4_f
bsbbr_3_t:
	wash2[0] = dispense(wash_buffer)
	washed2[0] = mix(selection_mix1[0], wash2[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	dispose(washed2[0])
	REPEAT_52[0] = REPEAT_51[0] - 1
bsbbr_4_f:
	elution1[0] = dispense(selection_buffer)
	eluate1[0] = mix(selection_mix1[0], elution1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	mastermix1[0] = dispense(pcr_mastermix)
	primer_mix1[0] = dispense(primers)
	pcr_reaction1[0] = mix(eluate1[0], mastermix1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	pcr_mix1[0] = mix(pcr_reaction1[0], primer_mix1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	heat(pcr_mix1[0]) @ 95.0CELSIUS @ 30.0SECOND
bsbbr_5_h:
	PHI REPEAT_201 = {REPEAT_200,REPEAT_202}
	PHI pcr_mix2 = {pcr_mix1,pcr_mix2}
	if REPEAT_201[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_6_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_7_f
bsbbr_6_t:
	heat(pcr_mix2[0]) @ 95.0CELSIUS @ 15.0SECOND
	heat(pcr_mix2[0]) @ 60.0CELSIUS @ 30.0SECOND
	heat(pcr_mix2[0]) @ 72.0CELSIUS @ 30.0SECOND
	REPEAT_202[0] = REPEAT_201[0] - 1
bsbbr_7_f:
	heat(pcr_mix2[0]) @ 72.0CELSIUS @ 300.0SECOND
	exo1[0] = dispense(lambda_exonuclease)
	digestion_mix1[0] = mix(pcr_mix2[0], exo1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	heat(digestion_mix1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 1800.0SECOND
	heat(digestion_mix1[0]) @ 75.0CELSIUS @ 600.0SECOND
	assay_beads1[0] = dispense(target_beads)
	binding_mix1[0] = mix(digestion_mix1[0], assay_beads1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	heat(binding_mix1[0]) @ 23.0CELSIUS @ 3600.0SECOND
bsbbr_8_h:
	PHI assay_washed1 = {assay_washed0,assay_washed2}
	PHI REPEAT_41 = {REPEAT_40,REPEAT_42}
	PHI assay_wash1 = {assay_wash0,assay_wash2}
	if REPEAT_41[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_9_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_10_f
bsbbr_9_t:
	assay_wash2[0] = dispense(wash_buffer)
	assay_washed2[0] = mix(binding_mix1[0], assay_wash2[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	dispose(assay_washed2[0])
	REPEAT_42[0] = REPEAT_41[0] - 1
bsbbr_10_f:
	pool_signal1[0] = detect(fluorescence, binding_mix1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	if pool_signal1[0] >= 50	|	true: jump bsbbif_11_t	|	false: jump bsbbif_12_f
bsbbif_11_t:
	dispose(binding_mix1[0])
bsbbif_12_f:
	dispose(binding_mix1[0])
	jump: bsbbif_13_j
bsbbif_13_j:
	NOP

numeric_mismatches.field: single representative selection round (not three full rounds)
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper performs three rounds of selection per target with increasing stringency (lower target concentration and longer/higher-flow-rate washing in later rounds); this .bs file models one generic round rather than three parameterized rounds, since BioScript has no primitive to vary flow rate or bead/target quantity between iterations.

numeric_mismatches.field: repeat 5 times (MMS wash) / repeat 4 times (assay wash)
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper specifies wash duration (6 min round 1, 20 min rounds 2-3) and flow rate (50 mL/hr), not a discrete wash-cycle count; the repeat counts here are illustrative stand-ins, not literal paper values, since BioScript has no time/flow-rate-based wash primitive.

The paper describes pilot PCR to determine the optimal amplification cycle count without accumulating byproduct, but does not report a single fixed cycle number for the modeled step; 20 cycles is a typical/illustrative value.

Both branches perform the same disposal action because BioScript has no differential on-chip action for 'advance to cloning' vs. 'discard pool' - cloning/sequencing happens off-chip. The branch exists to represent the paper's affinity-based decision point, not to model distinct on-chip outcomes.

numeric_mismatches.field: pH-variation selection on PDGF-BB (Fig. 5), 75-aptamer literature comparison (Fig. 6), electrostatic surface mapping, isoelectric focusing, filter-binding cross-validation
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. These are downstream comparative-analysis, structural-modeling, or orthogonal-assay validation sub-experiments run alongside the core three-round selection protocol, and fall outside the scope of this translation.

metadata.notes: This protocol details Microfluidic SELEX (M-SELEX) for Rapid Generation of High-Affinity DNA Aptamers Against Protein Targets of Varying Isoelectric Point (PDGF-BB, Thrombin, Apolipoprotein E3). The assay is performed on a qPCR Thermocycler platform. Key reagents used in the assay include Randomized ssDNA Library and Target-Coated Magnetic Beads.
